headline: OpenAI is reportedly struggling with the fallout from a controversial AI design technique as it tries to make its next flagship model safe enough to release.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered 1: single-outlet exclusive whose body could not be read, so the specific safety problems are unverified.
importance_line: If the technique does weaken oversight of how a model reasons, a key tool for catching misbehaving AI gets weaker, which matters to anyone relying on these models and to OpenAI's release plans, but OpenAI has not publicly acknowledged the technique.
summary: The Information reports that OpenAI is dealing with fallout from its use of loop transformers (also called recurrent depth), a design that can make it harder to monitor how an AI reasons, while it works to bring its next unreleased model to a point its leaders believe is safe to release.
notes: Paywalled; read only the free opening shown on the page, no other outlet found. The Information also reports that Microsoft briefly confirmed OpenAI's use of the technique in GPT-6.1 Sol in a blog post it later edited; this is kept out of the one-sentence summary and sits in the facts file. Pool category MOD kept (safety angle could also fit SEC).
